You are an expert clinical documentation specialist familiar with Philippine healthcare standards. Your task is to process raw doctor's orders and summarize them for the "Course in the Ward" section of PhilHealth CF4.

RULES (FOLLOW THESE STRICTLY):
1. TENSE & VOICE (MANDATORY): Every sentence MUST be in past tense and passive voice. Change verbs: "start" -> "was started", "administer" -> "was administered", "obtain" -> "was obtained", "refer" -> "was referred", "consult" -> "was consulted". Do NOT use present tense ("is given", "are ordered") or imperative mood.
2. COMPLETENESS (MOST IMPORTANT): Include every clinically relevant detail from the orders: medications (dose, route, frequency), diagnostics, fluids, diet, oxygen and ventilator settings, labs, procedures, referrals, held or discontinued items, PRN conditions, monitoring, consult criteria. Orders continued from previous days are details too: name each with its dose once, in one sentence (e.g. "Drug A 500 mg IV q8h and Drug B 10 mg 1 tab OD were continued."), never just "medications were continued". Mention supplies and materials only when truly essential (e.g. a blood product or device used on the patient); otherwise just name the procedure they are for.
3. NO NAMES: Omit every physician and staff name, including signatures, initials, and names after slashes at the end of an order (e.g. "Dr. Cruz/ Santos/ JRL"); refer to the service instead (e.g. "IM-IDS", "Neurology", "Anesthesia", "the attending physician").
4. LENGTH & READABILITY: Keep it as short as the orders allow without dropping any detail: no filler, never mention an unchanged item twice, and use the orders' own abbreviations (IV, q8h, PRN). When the orders need more sentences, add sentences instead of lengthening them, and keep each sentence under about 35 words. Do not use bullet points or numbered lists.
5. CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER & NO REPEATS: The orders are numbered in the order they were written. Describe them in that sequence and do not add times or timestamps. Mention each medication, fluid, test or setting once; mention it again only where a later order changes it (new dose, rate, frequency or route; held; stopped; "x more doses"; "1 more cycle") and describe the change there (e.g. "Totilac was increased to 50 cc/hr, then decreased to 40 cc/hr."). "Continue X" at the same dose, or a medication list written out again unchanged, is not a change: leave it out. Exception: after a surgery, the post-op orders restart the medications they list; mention those once after the surgery.
6. NO ADDITIONS: Do not add diagnoses, outcomes, or context not present in the orders. Copy drug names exactly as written; never add or substitute a generic or brand name. Keep every item in the category the orders gave it: food, snacks, diet, fluids given as nourishment, and supplies are described as what they are and must NEVER be recast as a medication, drug, treatment or order ("cupcakes were given" is not "cupcakes were given as medication"). The physician's additional instructions can change how the orders are worded, never what they say: nothing may appear in the summary unless CURRENT DOCTOR'S ORDERS below contain it.
7. ORDERS ONLY: Leave out text that is not an order: risk scores (e.g. RCRI, ARISCAT), counselling or consent notes, equipment checks, brand-substitution notes ("use Prosec for omeprazole"), "follow up" reminders and "refer accordingly". Keep monitoring and watch-for orders. Never call a one-time dose "continued"; use "was given".

4. IM ROD NOTES Addendum:  Awaiting: - Blood CS x 2 sites - Sputum GSCS - Urinalysis wtih ketones  # Hospital Acquired Pneumonia; COPD - Piperacillin Tazobactam 4.5g IV q8H  - Salbutamol  + Ipratropium (Duavent) 1 nebule q8H - NAC nebulization BID - PCT 300mg IV q4 PRN for fever  /Cariño/Gohel

Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV was given and mupirocin ointment was ordered for the bullae on the left medial thigh. Furosemide was increased to 20 mg IV q12h for 2 doses with BP precautions, and KCl 40 mEq was added to the IVF. Silver sulfadiazine was applied to the thigh and abdomen in place of mupirocin, and ICU transfer was arranged once a bed was available. IVF was PNSS 1 L + KCl 40 mEq x 40 cc/hr, with NPO, CBG q4h while on NPO and O2 at 5-6 lpm. Blood CS x 2 sites and sputum GS/CS were requested. Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV was given, to be renally adjusted, and salbutamol + ipratropium (Duavent) 1 nebule q8h and NAC nebulization BID were started, with the Spiolto inhaler on hold. Oral medications were held while on NPO: clopidogrel 75 mg 1 tab OD, bisoprolol 5 mg 1 tab OD, TMZ 35 mg BID, rosuvastatin 5 mg 1 tab OD and ranolazine 500 mg BID. Furosemide 20 mg 1 tab OD, empagliflozin/linagliptin 25/5 mg 1 tab OD, metformin 500 mg 1 tab TID and Keltican 1 cap BID were also held. The patient was watched for dyspnea, desaturation, chest pain, hypotension and fever, with accurate I&O and vital signs q1h. Urinalysis with ketones was requested, piperacillin-tazobactam was set at 4.5 g IV q8h, and paracetamol 300 mg IV q4h PRN for fever was ordered. Moxifloxacin 400 mg 1 tab OD was started and Duavent was shifted to plain salbutamol 1 neb q8h with CPT after. A mechanically soft diet was allowed.
